weighted_dilation_norm_equivalence.eta_zero_singularity_and_operator_scope_: For eta > 0, Minkowski's triangle inequality yields finite mutual upper-bound multipliers zeta(1 + 2*eta) and zeta(1 + 2*eta)/zeta(2 + 4*eta). As eta -> 0^+, zeta(1 + 2*eta) = 1/(2*eta) + O(1) and zeta(1 + 2*eta)/zeta(2 + 4*eta) = 12/(tau^2 * eta) + O(1) (since zeta(2) = tau^2/24) because sum_{d>=1} d^{-1} = infty and sum_{d>=1} |mu(d)| d^{-1} = infty. Divergence of a triangle-inequality upper bound shows only that the Minkowski estimate fails at weight eta = 0; independently, by Mellin-Plancherel on L^2((0, infty), dX/X) along z = i*b (b in R), the square-dilation operator acts by the spectral multiplier sum_{d>=1} d^{-1 - 2*i*b} = zeta(1 + 2*i*b), which has a pole at b = 0.

mellin_identities.rh_equivalence_explanation: For z = a + i*b with a, b in R, Cauchy-Schwarz on int_0^infty Q_a(X) X^{-z} dX/X with eta = a/2 in (0, 5/4) (or Mellin-Plancherel along a = eta in (0, 5/2)) shows that finiteness of ||Q_a||_eta for all eta in (0, 5/2) forces M[Q_a](z) to be holomorphic throughout 0 < a < 5/2. Since Gamma(5/4 - z/2) and zeta(1 + 2*z) have no zeros in 0 < a < 5/2, any off-critical zero rho = x + i*y of zeta(s) with 1/2 < x < 1 creates a non-removable pole at z = rho - 1/2 with Re(z) = x - 1/2 in (0, 1/2) subset (0, 5/2).
mellin_identities.bridge_to_subgate_tc_043a_explanation: TC grades K remain real algebraic (K in A_R); auxiliary positive real scales and real norm weights eta > 0 do not automatically become TC grades. For integer dilations d >= 2, Lindemann's theorem (tau = 2*pi is transcendental) implies tau^q != d^2 for every nonzero rational q in Q \ {0}, establishing that log_tau(2) and log_tau(d^2) are irrational (not in Q). Irrationality does not exclude algebraic irrational grades in A_R \ Q, and whether log_tau(2) or log_tau(d^2) belongs to A_R is unestablished here and unnecessary: the weighted norm ||.||_eta is defined on the continuum L^2((0, infty), X^{-2*eta} dX/X), which is partitioned into the tau-adic intervals [tau^k, tau^{k+1}) indexed by rational integer grades k in Z subset A_R.

section_5_transition_poisson_summation.poisson_summation_hypotheses_and_non_sch: The even function f(v) = v^{-6} exp(-1/v^2) (v != 0), f(0) = 0 is NOT in the Schwartz class S(R) because v^6 f(v) = exp(-1/v^2) -> 1 != 0 as |v| -> infty. Instead, Poisson summation holds by the following proved hypotheses (DLMF 1.8.14): (1) f in C^infty(R) with f^{(j)}(0) = 0 for all j >= 0 since lim_{v->0} v^{-m} exp(-1/v^2) = 0; (2) by induction, f^{(j)}(v) = P_j(v^{-2}) v^{-6-j} exp(-1/v^2) = O(|v|^{-6-j}) as |v| -> infty, so f^{(j)} in L^1(R) cap C_0(R) for every j >= 0; (3) for each L > 0, the periodization P_L(x) = sum_{d in Z} f((x + d)/L) and its derivative P_L'(x) = L^{-1} sum_{d in Z} f'((x + d)/L) converge uniformly on x in [0, 1] by comparison with sum_{d!=0} |d|^{-6} < infty and sum_{d!=0} |d|^{-7} < infty, so P_L in C^1(R/Z) has an absolutely convergent Fourier series, yielding at x = 0: sum_{d>=1} d^{-6} exp(-L^2/d^2) = L^{-5} [c_0 + sum_{j>=1} hat{f}(j L)] with c_0 = 3 sqrt(tau/2) / 8.

corrected_dyadic_abel_bound.formula: |U_lambda(Y; M)| << M^{1/2} min(M / Y, (Y / M)^{5/2}) exp(-c * Phi(M))
corrected_dyadic_abel_bound.half_open_stieltjes_decomposition: U_lambda(Y; M) = L_lambda(2M^-) g_Y(2M) - L_lambda(M^-) g_Y(M) - int_M^{2M} L_lambda(t) g_Y'(t) dt, where g_Y(t) = Y^{5/2} t^{-3} exp(-Y^2/t^2) satisfies sup_{t in [M, 2M]} g_Y(t) << M^{-1/2} min(M/Y, (Y/M)^{5/2}) and int_M^{2M} |g_Y'(t)| dt << M^{-1/2} min(M/Y, (Y/M)^{5/2}). Multiplying by sup_{t in [M, 2M]} |L_lambda(t)| << M exp(-c Phi(M)) yields the prefactor M * M^{-1/2} = M^{1/2}.
corrected_dyadic_abel_bound.mellin_residue_refutation_of_old_M_neg_h: If the old M^{-1/2} prefactor held uniformly across dyadic blocks M = 2^j, summing over j >= 0 would give |Q_lambda(X)| <= sum_{j>=0} |U_lambda(X; 2^j)| = O(X^{-1/2}) as X -> infty. Together with |Q_lambda(X)| = O(X^{5/2}) as X -> 0^+, the Mellin transform M[Q_lambda](z) = int_0^infty Q_lambda(X) X^{-z} dX/X would converge absolutely and be holomorphic on -1/2 < Re(z) < 5/2, including at z = 0. This contradicts the proved simple pole of M[Q_lambda](z) = Gamma(5/4 - z/2) zeta(1 + 2z) / (2 zeta(1/2 + z)) at z = 0 with nonzero residue Gamma(5/4) / (4 zeta(1/2)) = -0.1551682265... != 0.

Since sum_{e|q} mu(e) = 1_{q=1}, all terms q >= 2 vanish identically and the identity collapses to Q_lambda(X)^2 = Q_lambda(X)^2, supplying no additional global cancellation by itself.

global_stieltjes_energy_proof.split_point_and_thresholds: For X >= 256 (so sqrt(X) >= 16 and log(log(sqrt(X))) >= log(log(16)) > 1), split the integral at t = sqrt(X): (i) on 1 <= t <= sqrt(X), |L_lambda(t)| <= t and 2 X^2/t^2 - 3 >= 2 X - 3 > 0, so X^{5/2} int_1^{sqrt(X)} t * t^{-4} (2 X^2/t^2 - 3) exp(-X^2/t^2) dt <= 2 X^{9/2} int_1^{sqrt(X)} t^{-5} exp(-X^2/t^2) dt = sqrt(X) int_X^{X^2} w e^{-w} dw <= sqrt(X) (X + 1) e^{-X}; (ii) on t >= sqrt(X) >= 16, applying the unconditional Korobov-Vinogradov-Walfisz bound |L_lambda(t)| <= C_KV t exp(-c_0 Phi(t)) <= C_KV t exp(-c_0 Phi(sqrt(X))) (derived either directly or from |M(y)| <= C'_KV y exp(-c'_0 Phi(y)) via L_lambda(t) = sum_{d <= sqrt(t)} M(t/d^2)) and substituting u = X/t gives X^{5/2} int_{sqrt(X)}^infty |L_lambda(t)| |d/dt(t^{-3} exp(-X^2/t^2))| dt <= C_KV (1/2 + 2 exp(-3/2)) sqrt(X) exp(-c_0 Phi(sqrt(X))) << sqrt(X) exp(-c_1 Phi(X)). attack_A_coprime_euler_series_and_separa.off_critical_pole_non_cancellation_theor: For any hypothetical off-critical zero rho = x + i*y of zeta(s) with 1/2 < x < 1, at the conjugate pair (u, v) = (rho, conj(rho)) one has Re(2*rho) = Re(2*conj(rho)) = 2*x > 1 and u + v = 2*x > 1. Because zeta(w) has an absolutely convergent nonvanishing Euler product on Re(w) > 1 (with |zeta(2*rho)| >= zeta(4*x)/zeta(2*x) > 0 and zeta(2*x) > 1), neither the numerator zeta(2u) zeta(2v) nor the coprimality factor 1/zeta(u+v) can vanish at (rho, conj(rho)) to cancel the off-critical poles of 1/(zeta(u) zeta(v)).

replacement_theorem_global_super_polynom.remaining_barrier_to_subgate_tc_043a: Three distinct energy regimes must be kept strictly separate: (i) the unconditional all-logarithmic upper bound E_lambda(Y) <<_D Y (log Y)^{-D} (Y >= 2) proved here from Korobov-Vinogradov-Walfisz summatory cancellation (which is an upper bound, NOT an asymptotic for E_lambda(Y)); (ii) a fixed power saving E_lambda(Y) << Y^{1 - eta} for a single eta > 0 (for which a zero-free strip Re(s) > 1 - delta_0 is sufficient via Mellin contour shifting, without claiming necessity); and (iii) the full SUBGATE-TC-043A target forall eps > 0, E_lambda(Y) <= C_eps Y^eps, which is equivalent to finiteness of ||Q_lambda||_eta for all eta in (0, 5/2), holomorphy of M[Q_lambda](z) on 0 < Re(z) < 5/2, and RH.
